title: Part Three, Chapter 1: The Maize of Paxil and Cayala

verses.t: And here begins the account of when it was decided to make man, and of the search for what should be man's flesh. And the Creators and Formers, Tepeu and Cucumatz, as they were called, said, "The time of the dawn has drawn near, for everything to be completed and perfected, and for those who will sustain us to be made, the enlightened vassals; the living men of the earth have dried up," they said. They came together and gathered in a body, and went to take counsel in the darkness of the night; and searching, they took counsel and consulted, and grew sad here. And so their wisdom came out into the light, and they found what they were looking for, what should be man's flesh; and little time was left before the sun, the moon and the stars should dawn above the Formers.

From Paxil and from Cayala, as they were called, came the yellow ears of corn and the white ones. And these are the names of the animals that brought the food: the wildcat, the coyote, the parakeet and the crow. These four animals showed them the yellow and white ears of corn, which were brought from Paxil, which was a paradise, and they showed the road to Paxil; and this was how they found the food. And from this was made the flesh of the man who was formed, and this was man's blood; and this was put in by the Creators, those ears of corn. And so they rejoiced at having found a beautiful land, full of sweet things, of many yellow and white ears of corn, much pataxte and cacao; the sapotes, the anonas, the jocotes, the nances, the matasanos and the honey could not be counted. Everything was full of delicious foods in that town of Paxil and Cayala, as it was called, and there were foods of every kind, small and great, plants small and great; and the road was shown by the animals. And then, grinding the yellow and the white ears of corn, Xmucane made nine drinks; and food and drink went in, and then the fat and stoutness of man was created, when the Formers, who were called Tepeu and Cucumatz, made him. And then they set about creating our first fathers and mothers; and only yellow and white ears of corn were their flesh, and only food were the arms and legs of men, our first fathers. Four were those created, and only food was their flesh.
